free_turn.about: Rules 1.90 items 7805, 7806 (Leon, 20 Nov 2026: "if you win you get a free turn, if you lost the enemy get a free turn. The approach phase is out entirely"): a fight may open with one side's free turn (combat.ts startCombat extra.freeTurn; Survival's ambush, survival.json ambush): every unit of the other side sits round 1 out (Unit.waitRound 2), but a unit whose stat ambush_immune holds (Tremor) and one with ambush_ap, which keeps its first turn with that many AP (Shoot First). `ap`: the free side's first turn at most this many AP (null: a full turn; the number to soften it with). The log: `side` once ({units}: who sits out), `immune` and `ap` per unit, `sits` for each turn passed. (Retired: rules 1.64 item 5008's approach and rules 1.82 item 7004's Surprise, superseded by rules 1.90 item 7800.)

actions.text: each AP buys your Movement in tiles; a difficult-terrain tile counts double; paid-for tiles not yet walked carry over to the rest of the turn; cost = ceil((tiles - carried) / Movement)
move 3 x Movement tiles
move 1 tile, provokes no opportunity attacks
drop prone or stand up
light melee/unarmed 2 AP; heavy melee 3 AP
single shot or loose an arrow
3 rounds at one target, two rolls; the second roll at -4 to hit (a Quick weapon -3; a Heavy weapon that is braced -1). Rules 1.18

actions.area_built: every enemy ahead of the shooter within 1.5 tiles of the line to the target (a weapon with Wide Spray: its auto_width + 0.5), at any range the weapon reaches. Cone or corridor is open: spec item 1502
actions.text: one roll per target
speed reload: swap in the fullest spare magazine, the old one drops into the pile on your tile; or swap an Evoker core
tactical reload: the old magazine goes back in the pack, rounds still in it
use an item, open a door
draw from the pack into one hand (a one-handed weapon, a focus, a torch, a shield); what the hand held goes to the pack
draw a two-handed weapon: it fills both hands, what the off hand held goes to the pack
swap main hand and off hand
put away what a hand holds into the pack: 1 AP a hand, 2 for a two-handed weapon
drop what a hand holds: it lands in the pile on your tile
put on or take off a light armour piece (1.2 kg or less), each; heavier armour isn't changed in a fight
fit a mod to the main-hand weapon
pick up any or all of the pile on your tile or an adjacent one
reveals HP, armour, resistances, weak points
hold AP for one shot at the first enemy that moves into your line

actions.note: an Atheist prays too, by dice, with no patron (rules 1.6: Atheists and pilgrims)

persuade, threaten or parley (skill check)
put out Burning

attack_reveal.note: rules 1.61 (0.30, the shot that shows; item 4963): a unit that makes an attack is seen by every unit of its target's side until the start of its own next turn ('attacker_turn_start'; 'off' turns the rule off). A Hidden unit is untouched: Shadow decides. PROVISIONAL

full.note: rules 1.61 (0.30, cover beside you; item 4960): full cover beside the target on the side facing the shooter (and the line misses it) takes this off the shot; on the line it still blocks sight. PROVISIONAL

One function: combat.ts coverFor
facing.note: rules 1.61 (0.30, cover beside you; item 4960): a cover object on one of the eight tiles round the target counts when the direction from the target to it is within arc_deg of the direction to the shooter and it is nearer the shooter; a diagonal tile counts as `diagonal` cover at most. One function: combat.ts coverFor. PROVISIONAL

A save stores the class number: a class is appended, never inserted. penalty.no_sprint: no Sprint; armoured: counts as armour where a target's armour is asked (a unit with no sheet: at least the smallest armoured value); light_cap: the row whose value caps 'armour counts as at most Class I's' (Forlorn Hope); forge_fit: the Forge fits it (rules 1.91 item 7952); family, form: the tag fields (item 7900).
armor.other_slots: head, hands, footwear etc. carry per-item effects

combat.elemental_taken_cap_note: PROVISIONAL. Rules 1.70 item 5540 (Leon, 19 Nov 2026): the most elemental damage taken off, from every source together (Pain Threshold's +6% a point, at most 60%, and the rest from gear and traits); one number, read by character.ts elementalCap wherever the cap applies.

yield.disabled_text: cannot yield: disabled, no mercy shown
yield.spare_preview: It cannot yield: a blow that takes its last HP disables it, and no mercy is shown (no Clean Hands shield, no Mercy Devotion).
yield.note: Rules 1.66 item 5200: the one answer to can this enemy yield (surrender, Spare, Clean Hands, the Mercy vow, Love Conquers, a Narrator surrender).

focus_memory.note: rules 1.61 (0.30, focus memory; item 4964): the one enemy doctrine (combat.ts enemyRank, physical/ai.ts aiTechnique) counts a target its side has already attacked this round as less worth it: per_attacker (a share of max HP) added to its key for each other attacker of its side, and a technique's want x 1 / (1 + per_attacker x attackers). A tier's enemies.json `focus_memory` overrides per_attacker. No penalty against a Taunt, nor on a target at or below finish_share of its max HP. Rules 1.79 item 6703 (spec 4969 a): carry, the weight of each attacker of the round before (the side's memory past the round: the first foe of a round spreads too); built and OFF (0): any carry from 0.25 moves the enemy table's guard (test/balance/defence-measure: the idle pair's first Down 4.2 rounds at most, measured 5), for the lead. PROVISIONAL

health_look.about: How a creature's health reads to a side that has not Analyzed it (rules 1.3; rules 1.55 item 29): one word from this ladder and nothing else (no bar, no number). A rung holds while the creature's share of its HP is above `above`; `full` is at full HP only; a living creature below every rung takes the last. A side's own and an Analyzed creature read exactly (the bar and the number). `tone` is the colour family the screen pairs with the word: calm, or hurt (the HP red), or dire (the HP red, filled). `short` is the rung's short form (rules 1.55 item 43): the fight map's token chip shows it when the full word would run into a neighbouring token's chip; the full word everywhere else. A token at full HP shows no chip (the target card and the turn strip still say the word).
health_look.source: rules 1.55 item 29 (Leon's playtest and ruling, 15 Nov 2026)

shield_look.about: How a unit's shields read on screen (0.30.0; Leon, 16 Nov 2026: one bar made every shield look like one sum). The engine's screenViews.ts shieldsView is the one place it is worked out, in the order the damage path spends them (effects/damage.ts shieldOrder). `base` is the unit's one shield (Tending's Shield, the Sigil WARD, the Outburst's Shell and Inverse, a prayer's, a perk's: every gift that is not a layer); `layer` is a shield on a layer of its own (a class move's effect with `layer`: its name and its class's attribute are that move's and class's); `guard` is the Guard pool's line: how it soaks (its phase, a plate's worth, the plates kept back) is physical/guard.ts guardSoakOf, the copy the damage path spends by; `after` is Durability's Guard, `before` the Defender's Reactive Plate, `off` a soak switched off by its policy. A side's own units and an Analyzed creature read exactly; any other creature's shields read by name with a size word from `size`: its share of the unit's max HP, a rung holding while the share is at or below `upto` (the last rung: above every one); `bar` is the share of max HP the token's strip draws a rung at. `rule` is the one line the target card and your own panel print. The texts' {slots} are filled by shieldsView: {n} a number, {word} a size word, {name}, {by}, {what}, {plates}, {plate_word}, {per}, {keep}.
shield_look.head: SHIELDS

base.name: Shield
base.lasts: until spent or the fight ends, unless its giver ends it sooner
base.how: a new one keeps the larger of the two, unless its giver adds to it

layer.lasts: the rest of the fight, until spent
layer.how: its own layer, spent before the shield

guard.name: Guard
guard.after: met after the shields: it soaks what they leave, and true damage and hazards too, but never harm you do yourself or a condition's tick
guard.before: met first, before every shield: it soaks every blow and true damage too, but never the heart's own harm (its burn, the Mana Shock)
guard.off: its soak is switched off for this fight
guard.keep_unless_drop: {keep} kept back for a reaction, unless the blow would drop the unit

shield_look.absorb: Stops up to {n} of a blow before HP
shield_look.absorb_size: Stops a {word} amount of a blow before HP
shield_look.absorb_drop: Stops up to {n} of a blow that would take it down
shield_look.vs: The damage shown is before {what}: up to {n} is taken there first
shield_look.vs_size: The damage shown is before {what}: {word}, taken there first
shield_look.rule: A blow meets each layer in turn, the newest first, then the shield. Bleeding, burning and true damage go past every shield.

recoil.text: Recoil 2.0 (rules 1.56): each shot after the first in a turn is at minus the gun's Recoil (its `recoil` field with its mods': weapons_rules.gear_fields), cumulative, reduced by floor(Dexterity / dex_relief_per); halved (braced_mult, rounded toward 0) braced or Emplaced; none in a volley, a reaction or full auto.

gear_fields.about: Rules 1.56 (plan 0.29 primitive 2): the closed list of a weapon instance's number fields (character.ts gearNum). Each is a field of the weapon row (its own value, else `default`) and of a mod row (its change); `combine` sum adds every mod's to the weapon's, max takes the largest; a mod's `<field>_modes` limits its value to those attack modes.

recoil.about: the Recoil each earlier shot this turn adds (bows and the core rifle 0; the compensator -1)

magazine_pct.about: percent more rounds in every magazine of the gun, rounded down (the extended magazine)

bands.about: range bands past the effective range with no penalty against units (the red dot; the scope on aimed shots)

silent.about: 1: the gun's shots don't reveal a Hidden shooter (the suppressor)

melee_damage.about: the damage of a melee blow made with the gun instead of the fists' (the bayonet; the blow hits with the fists' skill)

quiver.rules: rules 1.53 (Leon, 14 Nov 2026): every archer may carry two quivers, one worn (arrows are drawn from it as part of the shot) and one ready; Switch quiver is a Drawn weapon's reload and costs a reload (actions.json costs.reload); a quiver is never refilled in a fight. A quiver's grade gives arrows held (items.json quiver.arrows) and nothing else; one enchantment a quiver (items.json, mod_slot enchantment).

heavy.about: Rules 1.92 item 8010 (Items 2.0 stage B): the Heavy word. A piece in a hand whose row carries the role tag `heavy` (its `tags`) takes `movement` from its holder's Movement (tiles per AP), added where held and worn gear is summed (character.ts gearEffects, which the one Movement reader reads); two Heavy pieces stack. The ram plate, the barrier wall and the pavise are Heavy; the riot shield keeps its own -0.5 and is not.

magazine_prices.about: Rules 1.42 (Core Rules, Ammo and calibres: empty magazines cost 30 for a pistol, 40 for a rifle, 25 for a speedloader, 60 for a drum or box). An empty magazine's price for a gun: by its reload unit first (speedloader, drum, belt), then by its category (pistol calibres 30, heavy boxes 60), else the default. A full magazine adds its rounds at the calibre's price (credits.ts priceOf).

special_round_price.about: Rules 1.56 (L2; was rules 1.42): a special round with a `price_mult` (items.json: armour-piercing x3, hollow-point x2, incendiary x3) is made, sold and carried by calibre: `rounds:<calibre>:<type>` costs `price_mult` x that calibre's round, and comes in the `calibres` listed here (the guns that are not bows, flamers, launchers or core rifles). `calibre` is the reference: a bare item id (`ammo_armor_piercing`, a 0.28 save's line, a loot row) reads as rounds of it. Enhanced rounds (no `price_mult`) keep their own price and fit any gun.

worn.about: Weapons v2, Durability rule 2 (moved from code by rules 1.50): a weapon or shield at this share of its full durability or less is Worn (guns jam on a natural 1 or 2, melee loses 10%); 0 is Broken. The screens' close-to-breaking mark (rules 1.50) is this state.

reloading.magazine: speed reload (cost_ap): swap in the fullest spare magazine; the one in the gun drops into the pile on your tile, empty or with its rounds and ammo type (spec items 679, 680)
reloading.tactical: tactical reload: the speed reload's cost + world_play.json pile.tactical_reload_extra_ap (1); the old magazine goes back to the spares in the pack with its rounds and type; not for a gun loaded round by round (spec item 679)
reloading.full: a magazine gun that is full isn't reloaded (Already full.)
reloading.off_hand: a character's off-hand gun reloads only from its own spares (or, loaded round by round, its loose rounds); an enemy's never runs out until stat blocks list it
reloading.loose: top up from loose rounds; nothing drops
reloading.enemies: carry the spare magazines their tier lists (Enemy stat blocks) and always speed-reload, so their magazines feed the piles (spec item 679)
reloading.pickup: a selection of the entries in the pile on your tile or one adjacent tile, everything by default (world_play.json ap.pickup; spec items 674, 675)

fx.note: Presentation only (the engine never reads it): how a weapon looks and sounds when it fires, by its effects family. A weapon's family is by_ammo[its ammo], else by_system[its phys.system] (a melee weapon, a focus blade included, is a blade when thrown), else by_category[its category]; the family's fields, then the weapon's own `fx` block over them (weapons.json), make its effects (apps/web/src/game/fx/weaponFx.ts fxOf). sound: the firing sample (apps/web/src/game/sfx.ts), one per round fired; rate: its pitch. look: what flies (bullet, pellets: a shell's cluster, arrow, lob: a grenade's arc, rocket, flame: a gout of fire, bolt: a charge's bolt, thrown: the weapon itself). mark: what a round that hits leaves (hole, pellets, shaft; none for a blast, a flame or a throw). blast: what goes off where it lands (frag, fire, smoke, flash, zap). shell: the casing thrown out; eject: when (shot: one a round as it fires; reload: all of them at the reload). mag: what drops on a reload. load: how a gun with no magazine takes its rounds (pump, break, cylinder, rounds). cycle: ms before the casing comes out (a pump, lever or bolt worked first). bow: bow (drawn from the quiver before each loose) or crossbow. spent_core: the spent core an Evoker of this weapon ejects (evoker, blade, staff). color: sigil or soul ink for the round. stand_in: the sample is a stand-in until a proper one is sourced (docs/design/handoffs/weapon-fx-table.md lists them).

launcher.stand_in: a 40 mm launcher's thump (the low boom pitched up for now)

conditions_rules.save: d20 + the target's save for the family (Body: Guts, Brain: Rumination, Heart: Composure) >= 12 + the strength of the skill that delivered the condition (its modifier, never below 0); a technique's own save adds half that strength, rounded up
conditions_rules.stacking: never stacks; reapplication resets to the longer duration

events.note: Rules 1.68 item 5403: three times the MP drawn (the bands' syphon_mp), three times the air it takes (was -2).

sigil.grammar: rules 1.4: at least 1 Subject and 1 other word; 2-4 glyphs in a straight Line (the only shape); one Reach word per spell; with no Reach word the spell is Touch (1 tile deep); full grammar in sigils.json
sigil.cost: draw: each word's charge + Glyph AP + 1 Flux; evoke: 1 AP + 1 charge per glyph - the core saving (skills.json brain_power per_point charge_at, character.ts sigilCoreSaving), min 1
sigil.hit: damage spells: brain_power vs defense; Afflictions: the target saves against 12 + the caster's strength with Brain Power; Boons and Workings: no roll
sigil.damage: the strongest damaging Subject in full + half of every other damaging glyph (items 588, 589) x Reach x Burst x Delivery multipliers x 0.9 per repeated glyph x the Line multiplier (rules 1.17: 1.7 for 2 glyphs, 1.75 for 3, 1.8 for 4; a character's Lines only) x (1 + the Sigil bonus + the Elemental bonus for elemental damage: added, not multiplied); a critical x1.5, to x2.0 at most; no ceiling

design.ready_designs: soul_modules.json limits.ready_designs (a number block, read by character.ts readyDesigns)
design.second_school: a rider at half strength with its own option

soul.cost: (school base + modules + 10 if second school + tone cost) * band soul_cost_mult * (1 + soul_cost_pct/100), min 5

strain.limit: soul_modules.json strain.limit (a number block, read by character.ts strainLimit)
strain.decay: -1 at the start of every one of your turns, always
strain.burn: 8 true damage per point over the limit at the end of your turn

mana_short.effect: Stunned 1 turn; a held Outburst goes off wild with its element's stage-1 rider on your own tile; Strain stays, and the caster is in Mana Shock (soul_modules.json strain.shock) until it is back at the limit or the fight ends: {=shock_hp_share|pct}% of max HP at the end of each of its own turns in it from the turn after the Short (the Short's own turn pays the burn only), nothing lowers or raises it, no second Short while it lasts (rules 1.56)

calming: steady the heart (1 AP, holding) -1 and no swell next turn

soul.hit: damage: Bolt and Lance roll will_power vs defense (a critical x1.5, to x2.0 at most; the roll reads the level gap: rules 1.17); Wave, Burst and Aura don't roll; control/status: saves

cycle.pump_mp: 10% of the Begin's MP * the stage reached (10%, 20%, 30%, 40%), min 1; rules 1.24, provisional (soul_modules.json cycle.pump_mp)
cycle.swell: +1 stage and +1 Strain (+2 Flooded) at each of your turn starts while holding
cycle.note: rules 1.19: x0.8 at stage 0, +0.2 a stage; the Damage base is 40 for a character (36 before Leon's ruling of 12 Nov 2026) and 24 for an enemy caster (soul_modules.json damage); one free Pump a turn; each feeling once in an Outburst

prayer.note: Prayer, Devotion and its XP are in patrons.json (rules 1.6 and 1.6.1: Devotion XP, the tag caps, Whisper / Hymn / Miracle, overreach, Witnessed, vows, rites, leaving a patron). The rules 1.0 numbers once kept here (a level a rite, the patron's mood as a TN) are retired.

level_factor.from: rules.json output.level.mend (rules 1.36: its own column, M(L) x scale(L)), at the giver's level
level_factor.who: characters and the units that fight for them; an enemy caster's healing and shields grow through its own multipliers (rules 1.15)

round_limit.withdrawn: rules 1.23 (Leon, 12 Nov 2026): there is no round limit. Rules 1.20 held spells and prayers to half of a creature's max HP a round; healing is priced in AP now, and the enemies go for whoever mends the most.

brake.about: Rules 1.60 item 4640 (Leon's ruling ii, 16 Nov 2026), restated in spec item 5610: each Mend or Shield (Touch is cut, rules 1.75), and the Mender's Triage, a giver gives the same target in the same round costs its MP x `mult` for every one that giver already gave that target this round (the second x1.5, the third x2.25). Built at the one cost site (effects/cost.ts braked, with the price's target: rules 1.70 P3; the 0.32 merge). `actions` are the actions it brakes, `<item key>#<action id>`; `per` the window the gives are counted in.

medic.note: The medic's kit, each × Healing given × the level factor of the giver's level. Triage: 2 AP, next to you, once an ally a turn, no supplies (out of a fight, with time to work: × triage_out_of_fight_mult, once an ally a scene). A stim and Stim Throw: 1 AP and a dose (a stim, or a Supply). Rally: 2 AP, every ally within 4 tiles, once a scene. A Field Repair on an ally: 2 AP and a spare-parts charge, per point of Improvisation. Rules 1.36: a stim is the gate alone: stim_pct of its target's max HP at every level (gear, priced in credits).

tending.note: The enemy AI's healer weight. What a unit has healed and shielded for others over this round and the last is counted; under a tenth of the giver's own max HP it is not noticed. How hard each tier turns on the healer is its healer_focus in enemies.json (0: never; 0.5: the healer counts as hurt by half its max HP more; 1: the healer comes first, and a shooter steps for a line on it).

mending.text: Healing and shields from Sigil magic, Outbursts, prayers and the medic's kit grow with the giver's level, by the same factor that raises what enemies deal (×1.13 at level 6, ×1.38 at level 12, ×1.82 at level 20). Nothing limits how much a creature can be healed in a round. Enemies notice who is mending the squad and turn on them: Soldiers lean that way, Elites and Bosses go for the healer first. In an area shape a healing or shielding Outburst gives each ally ×0.4.

gate.note: Rules 1.36 (heal-shield-percent-spec.md section 4, Leon's 20%): every heal and shield action is at least a share of its target's max HP, counted up to hp x scale at the giver's level (the level 1 reference HP): 20% for a 2-AP action (the profiles' min_pct: mend, sigil_mend, soul_mend, tend), 13.3% for a Whisper and a 1-AP Raise, 33.3% for a Hymn and an intervention, times the action's own multipliers (stage, shape, Line, a heal in an area shape x0.4). It rounds up.

mending.cap_note: Rules 1.36: no single heal restores more than this share of its target's max HP (a Miracle is exempt; shields have no cap: one stands per layer).

gear_preview.about: Rules 1.42 (survival-spec section 4.2 item 14): the reference a gear card's numbers are measured against outside a fight: a foe of this tier with this weapon, at the holder's level, standing `range_tiles` away (or the weapon's effective range when shorter; adjacent for a melee weapon). gearpreview.ts.
gear_preview.name: Soldier

rarity.ladder: rules 1.91 (items 7905, 7906): the rows are the one grade ladder: `order` (0 to 4), the word (`name`), `sold` (false: no shop and no Forge ever gives it, a Boss reward only) and every number; `arm` multiplies a graded worn piece's armour value only (1 for every grade until stage C fits it, PROVISIONAL). A grade is the instance's (GearState.rarity), never the row's.
rarity.rules: rules 1.95 (the scale, step 1 of the 0.34 rebalance; tools/balance/bible/scale.json grades, ruling A9): the grade ladder adds damage and armour again: Fine +1 to hit and x1.15, Masterwork +2 and x1.3, Relic +3 and x1.5, Celestial +3 and x1.75; `arm` is the same step on a worn piece's armour value and on a plate's soak. A grade adds its mod slot and properties to the row's own in step 5 (ruling 54: no row loses a slot). PROVISIONAL

measure.note: Units for reading a measurement. Not targets: nothing is fitted to them and no test fails on them (Leon, 21 Nov 2026). The measuring tools in packages/engine/test/balance (npm run balance, or their own environment variables) read and report in these units; rules 1.94.
measure.unit: percent of what the normal-share plain rifle deals in one 6-AP turn on the simulator's range at the same level; a heal or a shield: unit_heal
measure.unit_heal: percent of the reference character's max HP (output.level.reference_hp) restored or shielded by one whole turn spent on the source, all in (rules 1.36)

rifle.note: the 100% unit: the plain rifle at a normal share (test/balance/builds.ts plain_gun), its shot read at the gun profile's pin: the profile at Attribute `pin` (7, the creation ceiling of an attribute, where output.profiles.gun equals the weapon profile's flat 1.5), whatever the build's own Agility. A fixed reference, so that a percentage moves only when something it measures moves (rules 1.61 G1: a gun's damage follows its shooter's Agility). Every measure reads it through test/balance/sim.ts atYardPin. The lead's ruling R1, 16 Nov 2026 (spec item 4720)

soldier_turn.note: what one Soldier of the fight's level takes off the plain rifleman in one of its turns, in HP in the level scale's units (heal-shield-pass.md 1.1; rules 1.36): the unit a heal, a shield or a denied turn is read in

control.note: reading a denied turn: a whole Soldier turn denied reads as one rifle-turn (100%); one AP off it a sixth of that; an Elite x1.4, a Boss x3

area.note: reading an area: its single-target reading plus half of it for each extra target it is expected to catch; cluster: the enemies a shape catches when aimed at one of a standard group, measured (refit-measure.ts cluster: levels 1, 6, 12, open ground, rounds 2 on)

over_time.note: reading damage over time: in full for 2 rounds, x0.75 for longer (the target dies or is cleansed)

full_assault.note: what the fire doctrine puts on one character in one round of the standard encounter (the Elite focused, three quarters of a Soldier-turn), in HP, x scale (rules 1.36, heal-shield-percent-spec.md section 2)

output.rules: the unified damage formula, stage (a): a re-expression, no number moved (12 Nov 2026)
output.formula: amount = (base + flat) x Stat x Level x own multipliers x (1 + target bonuses, capped at +100%); dealt = max(1, floor(amount) - armour); healing and shields go to their sinks

level.note: rules 1.95 (the scale, step 1 of the 0.34 rebalance; tools/balance/bible/scale.json columns): one row a level, 1 to 20. deal: what a character deals and everything measured in a character's HP (max HP, armour, a plate, cover, objects) rides it, x1.214 a level, x40 at level 20 (40^((L - 1) / 19)); the old `scale` column is gone and scaleOf reads deal. mend: heals and shields, the normal bar's growth (deal x the HP bracket of a normal share). mp: max MP and every MP price, 1 + 0.06 x (L - 1). enemy_damage: a Figment's HP rides the enemy damage column (enemies.json levels.table damage_mult is the same). reference_hp is gone (no reader).

profiles.note: Stat = k x (1 + attr x (each Attribute of the pair - 1) + skill x each Skill of the pair). Rules 1.26 (the re-fit; Leon: no damage slope on rolled attacks, skill buys accuracy, level buys damage): every profile has one of three shapes. AIMED (an action that rolls to hit: a weapon, a Sigil Line, an Outburst): no slope, k a constant, the Level term deal. LANDED (an action that always lands: a prayer, a heal, a shield): 0.06 a point of Attribute over 1 and 0.06 a point of Skill (all in at 7/7 is 1.25 times a normal share at 4/4), k a constant. FLAT (what has no dealer's skill: a grenade, a tick, a trap a character sets): k 1, the Level term deal. Each k keeps its system's normal share at level 1 where it was (weapon 1.5, sigil 1.7, soul 1.55, healing 1.18, blessing 0.956). Rules 1.27 (the heal re-fit, Leon 12 Nov 2026): a healer's turn all in is 2.0 Soldier-turns (was 1.25), so the heal and shield profiles were scaled by 1.6 and trimmed: healing and mend, soul_mend (the Soul shields) and the Sigil boon's sigil_mend (a Sigil boon also multiplies by Healing given, so most of its rise came through healing); blessing_mend is the heal dial of a prayer (Blessing power times blessing_mend.k over blessing.k), capped where a Hymn turn heals 2.5 Soldier-turns at level 1. Each heal and shield profile has a floor: never under that share of a normal share's Stat term (output.floor_reference).

floor_reference.note: Rules 1.27 (the heal re-fit; spec item 1733): a landed heal or shield profile with a floor (output.profiles: healing, mend, sigil_mend, soul_mend, blessing_mend) never has a Stat term under floor x the Stat term of a normal share, which is this many points in each Attribute and Skill of its pair. A damage profile has no floor.

weapon.from: weapons.json phys: each scales_with Attribute; the skill it hits with (also_scales when a weapon names it)

elemental.note: rules 1.95 (ruling 31): an elemental Sigil part reads the Line's own pair

figment.note: rules 1.95: the Figment door's pair (ruling 31); the elemental pair it read before is gone

guard.note: rules 1.95: a plate's soak reads the Guard door's pair (scale.json plate)

systems.note: Steps a4 and a5: each system's amount is its base x the Stat term x its own NAMED multipliers, every one a number in data; to re-fit a system, change the number where it lives. `where` names the field. `order`: the multipliers apply to the base one after another in this order; `round`: how the number is made whole.

sigil_damage.base: sigils.json items[word].damage (the strongest glyph in full, every other half; each damage type apart)
sigil_damage.stat: Sigil power: the Sigil multiplier, plus the Elemental bonus for Elemental damage (added)

own.shape: sigils.json: spread, chain, arc, twice, placed (a Burst's or a placed spell's multiplier on this creature)
own.line: sigils.json grammar.line_mult (by glyph count; a character's Lines)

sigil_boon.base: sigils.json items[mend].heal, items[ward].shield (heal_enemy, shield_enemy for an enemy caster)
sigil_boon.stat: the landed sigil_mend Stat (rules 1.26; the Sigil multiplier before)

own.healing given: the caster's Healing given (a second Stat term, as an own multiplier)

outburst_damage.base: soul_modules.json damage.base (damage.enemy_base for an enemy caster)
outburst_damage.round: none (harm floors it after the way of striking, a second school's half, the critical and the tone's riders)

own.stage: soul_modules.json cycle.stage_mult, plus feelings.json each feeling's step, the residue and resonance (added)

own.shape: schools[buff].area_mult in an area shape; items[split].boon_mult

prayer_damage.base: patrons.json: the prayer's stat_mod on hp (below 0), chain_damage, execute.boss_damage; an intervention's value + per_devotion x Devotion

prayer_mend.base: patrons.json: the prayer's heal or shield value; Mother Ember's intervention: its value + per_devotion x Devotion

kit.base: rules.json mending.medic (triage, stim, rally, field_repair_per_point x Improvisation)

magic_heal.base: what the spell or Outburst computed

amounts.note: Step a6: amount blocks that belong to no item (packages/engine/src/effects/amounts.ts, key rule:<name>). Every other block is on its item (`amounts`).

damage.text: rules 1.90 item 7808: a solo character's fumbled ambush (run/ambush.ts): a share of its own max HP, before round 1; no armour, Guard or item changes it, and it stops at survival.json ambush.fumble.floor_hp

heal.text: the Buff school riding a shelved class's own strike (classes/soul.ts)

output.text: Every amount of damage, healing and shield is one formula with its terms in data (packages/engine/src/effects/output.ts): the source's base, the Stat term of its profile (the character's Attribute and Skill), the Level term, the source's own multipliers, then the bonuses against this target. The derived multipliers of the sheet (Physical, a weapon's, Sigil, Elemental, Soul, Healing given, Blessing power) are the Stat terms of these profiles, and the level factor of healing and shields is the mend column. Nothing is fitted by a number in code.

rolls.note: Read by packages/engine/src/rolls.ts, the one place the engine rolls a d20 (engine foundations 1, 12 Nov 2026). The save base TN is conditions_rules.save_base_tn and the check ladder is resolution.tn_ladder; what is here are the other numbers a roll used to carry as a literal.

bosses.about: What makes a unit a Boss for the rules every item shares (the 0.29 consolidation, the lead's rulings of 16 Nov 2026): its tier or its kind (a Celestial). Read by combat.ts isBoss. A Taunted Boss is never forced to attack its taunter: it chooses, with the Taunted row's penalty against anyone else (conditions.json taunted). A forced move from an opponent never moves it (forced_movement.boss_holds).

boss_holds.about: A Boss (rules.json bosses) is never moved by an opponent's forced move (a push, a pull, a throw, a teleport, a swap: any item, weapon or technique); the knockback immunity and Nailed already hold any unit the data marks so. The one exception (rules 1.86 item 7405, engine lane: one rule, no list of items): a displace row that names `boss_tiles` moves an opponent's Boss at most that far (Tug's Bond, Pull Together's since rules 1.75 item 6213: 1 tile on a failed save).

guide.about: rules 1.33: Tending's Guide: an ally steps, willing, to the tile its Bonder picks (it provokes nothing)

break_not_persuade.resolved_as: a condition against a save: the speaker's strength with the skill that spoke against the target's save for that family

long.mp: full if meter band normal or richer

acquired.mastered: the skill's own Mastered perk, granted automatically

achieved.requires: Mastery 2 (5 points) in every listed skill + a deed in play
achieved.granted_by: the engine for the nine deeds it can watch in a fight (rules 1.14); the Narrator for the other ten, and the Narrator may still grant any of them by hand

ultimate.granted: automatically when holding both named Achieved perks

Echo totals and Overreach resist costs

writing voice hooks and voicing passed hooks
granting the Achieved perks whose deeds the engine cannot watch (it grants the nine fight deeds itself, rules 1.14; any may still be granted by hand) and recording deeds
setting the starting meter by location
keeping the Veil and the Knowing
Faith (rules 1.6): pacts, knowledge pieces, Narrator rites, Devotion XP moves for deeds (-6 to +5) and the day counter; the engine owns the tags, vows, Witnessed, interventions and the Miracles
trait and perk effects flagged narrator

item_tag_kinds_about: rules 1.91 items 7900, 7901: the closed list of item tag kinds. A tag is a kind:value string; general code asks for tags (packages/engine/src/itemtags.ts itemTags, itemsWith), never for an id. No explosive tag (the row field explosive) and no rarity tag (grade is the one value).

item_tag_kinds.about: the row's raw data category, as it is (light_melee, thrown, pistol, shield, armour, focus, mod...); no mapping table
the row's family (data/families.json); a row with no family is its own family; a variant is its base's; body armour: its class row's
the row's form: dex, hybrid, str (melee); close, standard, long (guns, bows); light, standard, heavy (shields, armour, heavy families)
the row's real-pattern word; art and collections only, no rules reader
the instance's grade (GearState.rarity; a unique's fixed grade); a row with no instance is standard
the slot of equipment_slots.table the row is worn or held in (the row's slot; a weapon row with none: main_hand)
words general code asks for, from the row's tags (lever, electronic, evoker_linked, natural; heavy: rules 1.92 item 8010, the Heavy word; issue: rules 1.93 item 8100, the camp's rack)
true on a unique variants line (rules 1.91 item 7917): never rolled

equipment_slots.table_about: rules 1.91 item 7908: the one slot table (id, the saved key Character.worn is keyed by, the label, the order); read by the engine and the client. The saved key wins: the inner torso slot is inner_torso (rules 1.91 item 7958; a save's older worn.torso_inner is moved on load).

veil.engine: record what is worn; apply nothing

equipment_slots.other_slots: each item lists its own small effects; none defined yet (spec 14 item 9)

zones.about: Classes 3.0 P10 and P9 (rules 1.78 item 6607): the kinds of zone data may lay (op zone; predicates self_in_zone, actor_in_zone, target_in_zone; engine: magic.ts DATA_ZONE_KINDS, makeZone, zonesAt). A row: id, the system that lays it. One side's zones of a kind on one tile never stack (rules 1.78 item 6601).

kinds.seat_note: rules 1.82 item 7005 (the seat): a Whisper of a unit of the zone's side reaches from any of its tiles as if the caster stood there (sight and range; faith.ts prayerSeats)

ties.about: Classes 3.0 P8 (engine: kit.ts tie, untie, tiesOf): the kinds of tie between two units. A row: id, max (a holder's base cap; the stat ties_max:<kind> adds to it; no max: no cap), ends_on (from_down, to_down, to_dead, unseen_round, combat_end), on_end (none, or unmake: the far end is unmade, P9), line (the map draws the tie: ink, and foe_dash, the dash pattern to a unit of another side; screenViews.ts tieLines). Each system adds its own kind.

kinds.about: Prayer 2.0 review fix (16 Nov 2026): a Chaplain's Canticle ties the singer to each ally its verses reached (from: the singer). When the singer is hurt, the break ends the verses only on the units tied to it, and every verse tie it holds; the song lapsing (a turn without singing) ends them too. No cap, no line.

Classes 3.0 P9: an owned unit (owned.ts): its owner is the from end. The drone, the beast and the twin are tied so, for the whole fight; a system that needs more ends (an owner going Down, an unmake) adds its own kind.
Rules 1.74 item 6041 (Visualization's fork Masterwork): the holder's one named Figment (from: the holder). At most one; it ends when the Figment goes down or the fight ends.

line.about: Classes 3.0 step 10 (Leon): a faint line on the map from the Bonder to each unit it is Bonded to while the tie lasts; Insight's ink; dashed to an enemy (the shape, not the colour alone, tells them apart). A kind with no line draws none.

kinds.about: Rules 1.33: a Bond. The cap is the stat ties_max:bond (Empathy 1, 5, 8; the Mender +1); the far end bears Bonded while tied; an enemy Bond ends on its Down or a round out of sight; an ally Bond holds while the Bonder is Downed from Empathy 10 (ties_keep:bond); all end when the Attuner leaves the Bonder's person.

shadow.about: rules 1.32 (shadow-spec.md): Perception's door, through Ingenuity. The meter on the unit (res.shadow): its cap by Ingenuity points, the Operative's own add and start, and the Break's one multiplier (1 + per_point a point spent + ambush_bonus on a fresh ambush + marked_bonus against an enemy you Marked). The door item (skills.json ingenuity.1) carries the Break's numbers; the validator holds them equal to these.

stale_state.about: Rules 1.86 item 7407 (engine lane; the gaps lane's group F item 17): per-character state that handlers removed before 0.29 left on old sheets (harmless, but nothing read or cleared it). The load door (game.ts migrateLoaded) deletes these keys: character: keys of a character's own state (c.state); story_items: an item key's keys in the story's per-character item state (story.ps[character].items[key]). Nothing is written when none is there.
